comment: D4 Round 25 — key backup encryption vectors. Spec authority: crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md (recovery-key envelope) + extensions/key-backup.md. Client encrypts megolm session keys + cross-signing keys + private device keys with a passphrase-derived recovery key (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with at-least 600k iterations + 16-byte random salt → 32-byte master key) before uploading. Server stores opaque blob keyed by (account_did, backup_version). Server NEVER sees plaintext. Restore: client downloads blob, re-derives key from passphrase + salt, decrypts. Rotation: client mints new (passphrase, salt, version) and re-encrypts all session keys; new uploads target version_new; server retains version_old until client confirms migration completion.

vectors.name: client_side_passphrase_derives_master_key
vectors.comment: Client derives the recovery master key locally from a passphrase + random salt via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 at >=600000 iterations. The plaintext passphrase NEVER leaves the client. Server sees only the derived encrypted blob.

expected.rationale: Client-side KDF: passphrase stays local; salt is uploaded with the blob so future restore can re-derive the same key.

vectors.name: server_side_blob_storage_opaque
vectors.comment: After client encrypts, the upload contains: {version_id, salt_b64, kdf_iterations, encrypted_session_keys_b64, ciphertext_nonce_b64, auth_tag_b64}. Server treats the encrypted_session_keys_b64 as opaque bytes and persists by (account_did, version_id). Server CANNOT decrypt without the passphrase.

expected.rationale: Zero-knowledge backup: server stores ciphertext blob + KDF parameters; cannot derive plaintext without the user's passphrase.

vectors.name: restore_path_redrives_key_and_decrypts
vectors.comment: Client restores: GET /api/v1/key_backup/blobs/{version_id} → re-derive master key from cached passphrase + downloaded salt + iterations → decrypt with ChaCha20-Poly1305 using nonce + auth_tag from blob → recover session_keys map. Successful decryption proves passphrase correctness AND blob integrity.

expected.rationale: Restore re-derives the same master key (deterministic given passphrase+salt+iterations); AEAD verifies integrity AND correct passphrase atomically.

vectors.name: rotation_mints_new_version_and_reencrypts
vectors.comment: User rotates passphrase. Client: derives new master key with NEW (passphrase_new, salt_new), re-encrypts ALL session keys, uploads to version_id_new. Server retains version_old until client sends migration_complete=true (or version_old TTL expires, default 30 days). Old version_id MAY be deleted after grace period; the rotation MUST NOT silently drop session keys (atomic re-encrypt + upload).

expected.rationale: Rotation is atomic re-encrypt + upload of every session key under the new master key; both versions coexist until migration confirmed.

negative_vectors.name: low_iteration_count_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: Client tries to upload with kdf_iterations=10000 (below the 600000 minimum). Server MUST refuse since this is a client misconfiguration that weakens the backup against offline brute-force.

expected.rationale: Backup blob KDF iterations MUST be >= 600000 (per spec); below this the passphrase is too easily brute-forced.

negative_vectors.name: wrong_passphrase_aead_rejects
negative_vectors.comment: Restore client supplies wrong passphrase. Derived master key differs; AEAD auth_tag verification fails; client MUST refuse to use any partially-decrypted data.

expected.rationale: ChaCha20-Poly1305 auth tag fails for any wrong key; client MUST treat partial decryption as failure (no plaintext leak).
